.gitignore: # Files with secrets, from the migration. See MIGRATION.md.
MIGRATION.md: dotkit setup created this repository (~/.dotfiles) from the Mac golden-mac on YYYY-MM-DD. This file lists what it carried over and what needs your attention. Work through the list, then delete this file and commit.
Setup uninstalled nothing that was on the Mac; the Homebrew packages stay installed. A file in the way of a dotkit link is renamed to <name>.before-dotkit.
| ~/.config/ghostty/config | config/ghostty.conf (~/.config/ghostty/config.local, read after the dotkit file) |
| ~/.gitconfig | config/gitconfig (~/.gitconfig, read after the dotkit file) |

These lines have a secret, so they are not in Git. They are in a file in local/ of this repository, which Git ignores, and the repository file reads it. On a new Mac, copy the file by hand, or keep its lines in a manager for passwords.
- config/ghostty.conf: Ghostty reads it after the dotkit settings. Delete the lines that you do not need to set again.
- config/starship.toml replaces the dotkit file config/starship.toml. Compare the two; the dotkit file has settings that yours does not, for example the Nerd Font symbols and the Git status.

- ~/.npmrc stays in place and outside the repository, because it has secrets (an npm token). dotkit does not link its own file there. To get the dotkit settings, copy them from config/npmrc of dotkit.
- config/gitconfig: Git reads it after the dotkit settings (config/gitconfig of dotkit). Delete the settings that are the same. Your name and email are in ~/.gitconfig.user.
Nothing to do: the dotkit base sets this up (Homebrew, completion, fzf, zoxide, Starship, mise, direnv, suggestions, syntax colors).
dotkit has completion, suggestions, syntax colors, and a prompt without a framework. Add the plugin lines you miss to config/zsh/zshrc. Remove the framework directory when you no longer need it.
Copy the block to config/zsh/zshrc if you still need it.
- ~/.bashrc: It stays in place. dotkit's ~/.bash_profile reads it in an interactive bash.
dotkit's zsh does not load them. Remove each one when you no longer need it.

mise replaces them; dotkit's shell does not load them. The base has Node 24, Python 3.14, and Ruby 3.4. A project pins its own versions with `mise use` or a .nvmrc, .python-version, .ruby-version, or .tool-versions file.
- nvm (~/.nvm): node v20.11.0 (default 20). With mise: `mise use -g node@20`. Then remove its lines from the shell files (the report lists them) and `rm -rf ~/.nvm`
mise installs these at the end of setup (`mise install`). The old copies stay, and they can come first in PATH. Remove each one when the mise copy works.
- `npm:typescript`, was 5.4.0 in nvm v20.11.0. Old copy: `npm uninstall -g typescript`
- `pipx:ruff`, was 0.4.0 in pipx. Old copy: `pipx uninstall ruff`
### Tools that are not in mise
They stay where they are. To add one to config/mise.toml:
- `pnpm` (nvm v20.11.0): dotkit has no global pnpm; each project supplies its own, with mise or corepack. `npm uninstall -g pnpm` when you no longer need it.
dotkit has these tools already, so they are not added.
- `bat` (cargo install): dotkit has bat (from Nix). Old copy: `cargo uninstall bat`
The dotkit base has these tools, so they are not in your lists. The Homebrew copy stays installed. Remove it when nothing else needs it; brew says when another formula depends on it.
- `ripgrep`: dotkit has ripgrep (dotkit, from Nix). `brew uninstall ripgrep`
- `node`: dotkit has node (dotkit, from mise). `brew uninstall node`
- `ghostty`: dotkit has ghostty (dotkit cask). `brew uninstall --cask ghostty`
These taps are not on GitHub, so the list has their URL. Check it.
These stay in place and keep working. To keep one in the repository, copy it to config/ and link it in nix/home.nix, for example `dotkit.links.".config/nvim" = "config/nvim";`.
config/bash/bash_profile: # Your lines for bash login shells, linked to
# ~/.bash_profile.local. The dotkit bash_profile sources it, then puts the
# global tool directories first in PATH.
# From ~/.bash_profile. MIGRATION.md lists the lines that are not here.
config/mise.toml: # Your global mise tools, linked to ~/.config/mise/config.toml. `dotkit add` and
# `mise use -g` edit it. The dotkit base (~/.config/mise/conf.d/dotkit.toml)
# has Node, Python, Ruby, uv, herdr, and the settings. A tool here replaces
# the same tool there, for example node = "22". Projects pin their own
# From npm, pnpm, and bun (global packages), see MIGRATION.md.
# From pipx and uv tool, see MIGRATION.md.
config/zsh/zprofile: # Your lines for zsh login shells, linked to ~/.zprofile.local. The dotkit
# zprofile sources it, then puts the global tool directories first in PATH.
# From ~/.zprofile. MIGRATION.md lists the lines that are not here.
config/zsh/zshrc: # Your zsh lines, linked to ~/.zshrc.local. The dotkit zshrc sources this file
# at the end, after the plugins and the base aliases. No rebuild needed.
# Lines with secrets, not in Git. See MIGRATION.md.
# From ~/.zshrc. MIGRATION.md lists the lines that are not here.
nix/brews.txt: # Homebrew formulae, one per line: only tools that Nix and mise cannot supply
# well. `dotkit add` selects the source and appends new ones at the end.
# From Homebrew on golden-mac, see MIGRATION.md.
nix/casks.txt: # Homebrew casks, one per line. `dotkit add` appends new ones at the end.
# From Homebrew on golden-mac, see MIGRATION.md.
nix/home.nix: # Home Manager settings of this Mac, on top of the dotkit base. Options:
# Your config files, as links: target in ~ = file in this repository.
# A target that the dotkit base also links (for example .config/starship.toml)
# replaces the base file. null removes a base link.
# Yours stays in place, see MIGRATION.md.
# Packages that need a Nix expression. Plain names go in nix/packages.txt.
nix/mas.txt: # Mac App Store apps, one per line: the App Store ID, then the name, as
# `mas list` shows them. `dotkit add mas:ID` appends one.
# From the App Store on golden-mac, see MIGRATION.md.
nix/taps.txt: # Homebrew taps for formulae and casks from other repositories, one per line:
# owner/repo. A tap that is not on GitHub has its clone URL after the name:
# A formula from a tap is owner/repo/name in nix/brews.txt.
# From Homebrew on golden-mac, see MIGRATION.md.
nix/user.nix: # Your macOS account and this repository. dotkit's scripts/setup writes it.
